```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`contentiousR` creates reproducible country-year panels for contentious politics and civil conflict research, offers diagnostics and visualization tools, and allows interoperation with `peacesciencer`.

## Build a panel and add data

First, load a package. Then, create a state panel with the selected temporal coverage and coutnry coding system. Use a pipeline workflow to add data, such as economic and conflict vaiables.

```{r}
library(contentiousR)

panel <- build_states_panel(
  start_year = 2000,
  end_year = 2002,
  coding_system = "cow"
)

analysis_data <- panel |>
  add_gdp() |>
  add_conflict("ucdp_prio") |>
  add_leader_data("archigos")

analysis_data[1:4, c(
  "country", "year", "gdp_pcap", "ucdp_prio_incidence", "leader"
)]
```
If there is an unmatched row, R returns `NA`

## Standalone workflow

If you want to inspect data before proceeding to further steps, standalone workflow can be helpful, as it loads data and saves it withint R environment.

```{r}
conflicts <- conflict_data(
  start_year = 2000,
  end_year = 2002,
  dataset = "ucdp_prio",
  coding_system = "gw"
)

head(conflicts)
```
See `vignette("data-sources", package = "contentiousR")` before interpreting any
source-specific variable.

## Conflict spells (peace-years)

`add_spell_duration()` helps one add peace spells, i.e. years since the last event for that state. This tool can be useful as a control for temporal dependence (e.g. with cubic splines). It needs a column without `NA`, so
filter first:

```{r}
spell_data <- build_states_panel(1990, 2005, coding_system = "gw") |>
  add_conflict("ucdp_prio") |>
  tidyr::drop_na(ucdp_prio_onset) |>
  add_spell_duration(event = "ucdp_prio_onset")

spell_data[spell_data$gw == 2, c("gw", "year", "ucdp_prio_onset", "ucdp_prio_spell")]
```

To work, the function needs an `event`; if it is omitted, `add_spell_duration()` looks for exactly one column ending in
`_onset`, `_incidence`, or `_ongoing` and uses that; but it errors if none or
several are found.

## Lagged variables

`add_lag()` adds a lagged version of one or more columns, computed within
each state after sorting by year and grouping by state before lagging. 
Unlike a plain dplyr::lag(), it also checks that the previous row really 
is the previous year. If a year is missing, say a country has data for 2002 
and 2005 but nothing in between, the lag for 2005 is set to `NA`.

```{r}
build_states_panel(1990, 1995, coding_system = "cow") |>
  add_gdp() |>
  add_lag(vars = c("gdp_pcap", "gdp_growth"), n = 1) |>
  dplyr::filter(cow == 2) |>
  dplyr::select(cow, year, gdp_pcap, gdp_pcap_l, gdp_growth_l)
```

Each requested variable gets one new column named `<var>_l`.

## Visualizing onsets

Use `plot_coverage` to visualize the treatment status across the panel data.
`1`s are shaded as an event, `0`s as no event, and years
where the source has no data — are left blank.  States that never have the event are 
dropped by default (`drop_empty = TRUE`)

```{r fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  build_states_panel(1990, 2015, coding_system = "cow") |>
    add_conflict("ucdp_prio") |>
    plot_coverage("ucdp_prio_onset")
}
```

## Quarterly, monthly, and daily panels

Set `unit = "quarter"`, `"month"`, or `"day"` to build a panel at a finer
unit. `add_conflict()` places each event in the period it started, annual
data such as GDP repeat across the months of a year, and leaders change in
the month they took office. With `fill_zero = TRUE`, months the dataset
covers but in which it records nothing get 0 instead of `NA`:

```{r}
monthly <- build_states_panel(2011, 2011, coding_system = "cow", unit = "month") |>
  add_gdp() |>
  add_leader_data() |>
  add_conflict("navco3.0", fill_zero = TRUE)

monthly |>
  dplyr::filter(cow == 651) |>
  dplyr::select(cow, year, month, gdp_pcap, leader, nvc3.0_n_campaign_events) |>
  head(4)
```

Only datasets that record exact start dates can be used at these units; see
the [data-source guide](data-sources.html) for which ones, how records
with imprecise dates are handled, and how coverage is defined for
`fill_zero`. `aggregate_panel()` collapses a finer panel back to quarters
or years, and `list_datasets()` lists every dataset with its coverage and
supported units.

## Working with V-Dem data

To work with the V-Dem data, download it from its official repository, then use only the indicators you need:

```{r eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("vdeminstitute/vdemdata")

panel |>
  add_vdem(c("v2x_polyarchy", "v2x_libdem"))
```

To get started, I will provide a detailed description on two functions: 
`load_gdp_data()` / `add_gdp()` and `load_population_data()` / `add_population()`.
For all other functions, see the
[Reference](https://rguseinov.github.io/contentiousR/reference/index.html)
page, which documents every function in the package.

## `load_gdp_data()` / `add_gdp()`

Two GDP sources are currently supported and maintained: `"gapminder"` and `"fariss"`.
`"gapminder"` (default) returns
`gdp_pcap`, `log_gdp_pcap`, and `gdp_growth`. `"fariss"` returns the latent
GDP and GDP per capita estimates from Fariss, Anders, Markowitz, and Barnum
(2022)

```{r eval = FALSE}
# Standalone
gdp <- load_gdp_data(start_year = 1990, end_year = 2015, coding_system = "cow")
fariss_gdp <- load_gdp_data(1700, 2015, dataset = "fariss", coding_system = "cow")

# Pipeline
panel |> add_gdp()
panel |> add_gdp(dataset = "fariss")
```

## `load_population_data()` / `add_population()`

Three population sources are available via `dataset`.

| Dataset | Source | Coverage | Returned columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"wpp"` (default) | [UN World Population Prospects 2024](https://population.un.org/wpp/) | 1949–2023 | `wpp_pop` |
| `"nmc"` | [Correlates of War NMC v7.0](https://correlatesofwar.org/data-sets/national-material-capabilities/) (Singer et al. 1972; Singer 1988) | 1816–2022 | `nmc_tpop`, `nmc_upop` |
| `"fariss"` | Fariss et al. (2022) latent estimate | 1500–2019 | `fariss_pop` |

```{r eval = FALSE}
# Standalone
pop_wpp <- load_population_data(1990, 2015, dataset = "wpp", coding_system = "cow")
pop_nmc <- load_population_data(1900, 2015, dataset = "nmc", coding_system = "cow")

# Pipeline
panel |> add_population()
panel |> add_population(dataset = "nmc")
```

## Interoperate with `peacesciencer`

`contentiousR` supports `peacesciencer` (see Miller 2022). It means you can add data from `peacesciencer` 
within the same data construction pipeline. 

Functions such as `peacesciencer::add_archigos()` expect `ccode`/`gwcode`
keys plus attributes that describe the state system and unit of analysis. Use
`add_from_peacesciencer()` to return a panel with
only contentiousR's original country-code key:

```{r eval = FALSE}
library(peacesciencer)

analysis_data |>
  add_from_peacesciencer(peacesciencer::add_archigos)
```

For multiple additions, call `as_peacesciencer_panel()` once and
then apply the `peacesciencer` functions directly.

## References

Fariss, C. J., Anders, T., Markowitz, J. N., & Barnum, M. (2022). New estimates of over 500 years of historic GDP and population data. Journal of Conflict Resolution, 66(3), 553-591. [https://doi.org/10.1177/00220027211054432](https://doi.org/10.1177/00220027211054432)

Miller, S. V. (2022). {peacesciencer}: An R package for quantitative peace science research. Conflict Management and Peace Science, 39(6), 755-779. [https://doi.org/10.1177/07388942221077926](https://doi.org/10.1177/07388942221077926)

Singer, J. D. (1988). Reconstructing the Correlates of War dataset on material capabilities of states, 1816-1985. International Interactions, 14(2), 115-132. [https://doi.org/10.1080/03050628808434695](https://doi.org/10.1080/03050628808434695)

Singer, J. D., Bremer, S., & Stuckey, J. (1972). Capability distribution, uncertainty, and major power war, 1820-1965. In B. Russett (Ed.), Peace, war, and numbers (pp. 19-48). Sage.
